gap: r4's three items are genuinely closed: the headline now uses U+2019 ('What’s your'), the mark is /logo.svg vector in headline navy, and the card's filler rows are gone, replaced by the two facts a nervous buyer actually weighs (Card required today: None, Data if you leave: Yours to export). On desktop this now reads calmer and more confident than the bar's own home fold, which stacks a promo serif headline against the hero serif and crops a skewed dashboard off the right edge. It still does not clearly win, because the phone is where an SMB signup happens and the phone breaks. (1) The step labels carry a literal 'truncate' class, so step three renders as 'Modules & Payme…' at 390px. The third and final step of a money signup, the one that says Payment, is unreadable on the device most people sign up on. Wave never truncates a nav or step label. Drop 'truncate', let the row wrap to two lines or shorten the label to 'Modules', and reserve the ellipsis for nothing. (2) All three step labels are the same colour: active is 'text-ink-500 font-bold', upcoming is 'text-ink-500 font-medium'. Weight alone is not a state signal at 12px. The bar colour-codes state (the nav's 'Pricing' turns blue on the pricing page), so you always know where you are. Mute the upcoming labels to a lighter ink and let only the current step hold full navy. (3) On mobile the blue reassurance card sits BELOW the Continue button, so 'no card required today' and 'your data is yours to export' land after the decision they exist to de-risk. Move the card, or at least the two-row facts, above the CTA on the narrow breakpoint. (4) The card still says one thing twice: the row 'Data if you leave / Yours to export' and, four lines under it, 'your records exactly where you left them.' Cut the closing paragraph down to the one clause the row does not already carry, that stopping a paid module drops you to the free plan rather than closing the workspace.
